topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how studying transforming viruses established that cancer can originate through misregulation of normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how researchers test whether cancer-associated genes and mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Cancer-gene classification and mutation-specific function
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using RB regulation and dominant-negative p53 to illustrate and qualify those classifications.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect distinct patterns of cancer-genome instability to the fidelity and failure of DNA repair.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in transmitting the genome during cell reproduction generate instability and affect cancer-cell behavior.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutations and genetic instability influences the progression from normal colorectal epithelium to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inherited defects in cancer-control genes reduce the additional changes needed for tumor development.

topics.label: BRCA2 restoration and the persistence of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic uses treatment-associated restoration of BRCA2 function to demonstrate that continued genetic instability is not required for malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture close and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with an invitation for questions, a reading recommendation, and a preview of the next lecture.
